0.label: LLM Evaluation, Benchmarking & Applications
0.description: Research on evaluating, benchmarking, and applying large language models across diverse tasks, with emphasis on reliability, bias detection, and domain-specific adaptation.
subtopics: LLM benchmarking and evaluation frameworks
Hallucination detection and factual consistency
LLM bias, robustness, and reliability
Domain-specific LLM applications (education, engineering, translation)
Prompt engineering and fine-tuning methods

1.label: Domain Adaptation and Generalization Methods
1.description: Research on techniques for transferring, adapting, and generalizing learned representations across different domains, distributions, and tasks to improve model robustness under distribution shift.
subtopics: Domain generalization via data augmentation and synthesis
Unsupervised and weakly-supervised domain adaptation
Test-time adaptation and out-of-distribution robustness
Knowledge distillation and foundation model adaptation
Continual and incremental learning under domain shift

2.label: Multimodal Video and Human Understanding
2.description: Research on multimodal learning methods for video generation, human activity recognition, motion prediction, and visual understanding tasks involving video, text, audio, and other modalities.
subtopics: Video generation and controllable synthesis
Human activity and motion recognition/prediction
Multimodal fusion and video-language alignment
Egocentric and domain-specific video understanding
Human-centric 3D modeling and avatar generation

3.label: Efficient Transformer Model Optimization
3.description: Research on methods for compressing, accelerating, and efficiently adapting large-scale neural network models while preserving performance and accuracy.
subtopics: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning and adaptation (LoRA, PEFT, low-rank methods)
Model compression and pruning (MoE compression, structured pruning, knowledge distillation)
Efficient inference and speculative decoding for LLMs
Hardware-aware deployment on edge and resource-constrained devices
Transformer architecture analysis and principled design

4.label: Robot Manipulation, Control, and Interaction
4.description: This cluster encompasses research on robotic systems spanning manipulation, perception, control, locomotion, and human-robot interaction, with emphasis on learning-based methods and novel sensing modalities.
subtopics: Learning-based robotic manipulation and policy learning
Robot perception via tactile, visual, and language modalities
Motion planning and control for diverse robot platforms
Human-robot interaction and communication
Bio-inspired and novel robot design and locomotion

5.label: 3D Scene Representation and Reconstruction
5.description: Research on neural and geometric methods for representing, reconstructing, rendering, and understanding 3D scenes and objects from various sensor inputs.
subtopics: 3D Gaussian Splatting for dynamic and static scene rendering
Neural radiance fields and implicit scene representations
3D geometry processing (normals, SDFs, point clouds)
3D-aware generation, stylization, and editing
3D perception for robotics (SLAM, localization, object pose estimation)

6.label: Deep Learning Theory and Methods
6.description: This cluster encompasses research advancing deep learning through novel theoretical analyses, architectural innovations, training methodologies, and learning paradigms aimed at improving generalization, efficiency, and applicability across diverse tasks.
subtopics: Generalization theory and bounds for deep learning models
Novel optimization methods and training algorithms
Few-shot learning, transfer learning, and continual learning paradigms
Efficient data representation: dataset condensation, quantization, and compression
Neural network architectures: spiking networks, equilibrium propagation, and tensor-based methods

7.label: Adversarial Attacks and Media Forensics
7.description: Research on adversarial attacks against deep learning models and detection/forensics of manipulated or synthetic digital media.
subtopics: Adversarial attack methods and robustness evaluation
Deepfake and synthetic image detection and localization
Backdoor poisoning attacks and defenses
Face recognition and anti-spoofing under occlusion
Image forgery localization and digital forensics

8.label: AI for Biomedical Signal and Image Analysis
8.description: This cluster encompasses research applying deep learning and AI methods to analyze biomedical signals (EEG, fMRI, neural recordings) and medical images for diagnosis, prediction, and clinical decision support.
subtopics: Medical image segmentation and classification
Neural signal decoding and brain activity prediction
Clinical prediction and decision support systems
Food and nutrition analysis using AI
Interpretability and uncertainty in medical AI

9.label: Multimodal Vision-Language Models and Benchmarks
9.description: Research on vision-language and multimodal models addressing cross-modal alignment, benchmarking, and diverse application domains including medical imaging, cultural understanding, and document analysis.
subtopics: Benchmarks and evaluation for multimodal/vision-language models
Cross-modal alignment and representation learning
Visual grounding, referring expression comprehension, and object localization
Domain-specific applications (medical, fashion, cultural, historical documents)
Prompt learning and fine-tuning strategies for VLMs

10.label: AI for Transportation and Autonomous Driving
10.description: Research applying AI and machine learning techniques to advance autonomous driving, traffic management, and intelligent transportation systems.
subtopics: Autonomous driving perception and planning
Traffic prediction and congestion management
Object detection for transportation (vehicles, pedestrians, signs)
Mobility resource allocation and demand forecasting
Vehicle safety and robustness in adverse conditions

11.label: LLM-Augmented Knowledge Retrieval and Reasoning
11.description: Research on enhancing large language models with structured knowledge, retrieval-augmented generation, and reasoning capabilities for domain-specific and complex information processing tasks.
subtopics: Retrieval-Augmented Generation improvements and variants (Dynamic RAG, Parametric RAG, GAG)
Knowledge graph and structured data reasoning with LLMs (SPARQL, Text-to-SQL, ontologies)
Domain-specific LLM adaptation and evaluation benchmarks (finance, biomedicine, education)
Multi-agent and multi-step reasoning for complex queries
Evaluation frameworks and benchmarks for RAG and knowledge-intensive QA systems

12.label: Reinforcement Learning and Sequential Decision-Making
12.description: This cluster encompasses research on reinforcement learning algorithms, bandit problems, and sequential decision-making under uncertainty, including theoretical analysis, safety constraints, robustness, and applications to optimization and multi-agent settings.
subtopics: Bandit algorithms and regret analysis (contextual bandits, clustering of bandits, Thompson sampling)
Safe and robust reinforcement learning (constrained MDPs, adversarial corruption, model predictive shielding)
Policy optimization and search (policy compression, inverse RL, risk-sensitive RL)
Bayesian optimization and automated algorithm design (transfer learning, hyperparameter tuning, LLM-based generation)
Applications of RL to combinatorial and routing problems (vehicle routing, network security, multi-agent foraging)

13.label: NLP and Language Model Applications
13.description: Research on language models, machine translation, text processing, and evaluation methods across diverse linguistic tasks and domains.
subtopics: Machine translation and multilingual NLP for low-resource languages
Large language model adaptation and instruction tuning
Text generation control, simplification, and readability
Evaluation metrics for translation and text quality
Language model interpretability and internal representations

14.label: Scientific ML and Time Series
14.description: Research advancing deep learning methods for scientific computing (PDE solving, physics-informed networks, surrogate modeling) and time series forecasting with emphasis on interpretability, efficiency, and uncertainty quantification.
subtopics: Physics-Informed Neural Networks and PDE solving strategies
Time series forecasting architectures and interpretability
Uncertainty quantification and conformal prediction
Symbolic regression and analytical solution discovery
Neural operator surrogates for scientific simulations

15.label: Diffusion Models & Image Generation
15.description: Research on advancing diffusion-based and generative image models through improved guidance, alignment, controllability, restoration, and downstream visual tasks.
subtopics: Reward-guided alignment and constrained optimization of diffusion models
Training-free inference-time guidance and controllability for image generation
High-resolution and efficient image restoration and generation
Multi-object fidelity, text rendering, and compositional image synthesis
Visual recognition architectures and image processing for downstream tasks

16.label: AI-Driven Anomaly Detection Systems
16.description: Research on machine learning and AI methods for detecting anomalies, defects, and unusual patterns across diverse domains including cybersecurity, industrial systems, medical imaging, and time series data.
subtopics: Time series and log-based anomaly detection
Industrial and infrastructure monitoring with digital twins
Zero-shot and weakly supervised visual anomaly detection
Adversarial robustness and security-aware evaluation of detectors
Multimodal and transformer-based detection frameworks

17.label: Recommender Systems Advanced Methods
17.description: Research on advanced techniques for improving recommender systems, including knowledge graphs, large language models, causal reasoning, multimodal integration, and bias mitigation to enhance prediction accuracy, diversity, and cold-start handling.
subtopics: LLM and knowledge graph integration for recommendations
Click-through rate prediction and user behavior modeling
Cold-start and long-tail recommendation challenges
Causal reasoning and bias mitigation in recommendations
Multimodal and retrieval-augmented recommendation methods

18.label: Graph Neural Networks and Applications
18.description: Research advancing graph neural network architectures, expressiveness, and their applications across domains including molecular science, drug discovery, and web-based systems.
subtopics: GNN expressiveness and theoretical limitations (WL tests, circuit complexity, higher-order methods)
Molecular and chemical applications (drug discovery, enzyme kinetics, metabolic stability, synthesis)
Graph self-supervised and contrastive learning frameworks
Scalability and efficiency (early-exit mechanisms, subgraph sampling, dynamic graph condensation)
Robustness and generalization (heterophily, OOD shifts, uncertainty estimation, weak supervision)

19.label: AI for Remote Sensing & Environmental Monitoring
19.description: This cluster encompasses research applying deep learning and computer vision techniques to remote sensing imagery, environmental monitoring, and real-world detection tasks across diverse domains including agriculture, weather conditions, and urban applications.
subtopics: Remote sensing image classification and object detection
Image restoration and fusion under adverse weather conditions
State-space models (Mamba) for spatial-spectral data processing
Few-shot and self-supervised learning for limited labeled data scenarios
Domain-specific detection applications (agriculture, wildlife, environmental monitoring)

20.label: Sign Language Recognition and Translation
20.description: Research on computational methods for recognizing, translating, and producing sign languages using deep learning, computer vision, and natural language processing techniques.
subtopics: Continuous sign language recognition architectures (CNN, GCN, transformer-based models)
Sign language translation and production (text-to-sign and sign-to-text)
Sign language datasets and benchmarks for diverse languages
Evaluation metrics and frameworks for sign language systems
Real-time assistive technology and deployment for accessibility

21.label: NLP Sentiment Analysis and Bias
21.description: Research on sentiment analysis, emotion recognition, bias detection, and discourse analysis using natural language processing and multimodal approaches.
subtopics: Sentiment analysis methods and multimodal fusion
Bias, fairness, and debiasing in language models
Emotion recognition and affective computing
Topic modeling and discourse analysis
Counterspeech, hate speech, and social NLP applications

22.label: AI Safety and LLM Alignment
22.description: Research on ensuring the safety, robustness, and alignment of large language models and AI systems through detection, defense, and evaluation frameworks.
subtopics: Jailbreak attacks and defenses for LLMs and VLMs
Safety guardrails and real-time risk detection frameworks
Model interpretability and safety mechanism analysis
Alignment strategies including steering vectors and unlearning
Auditing, benchmarking, and evaluation of AI safety properties

23.label: LLM Reasoning and Learning Frameworks
23.description: Research on enhancing large language model reasoning capabilities through reinforcement learning, structured logic, memory mechanisms, and evaluation methodologies.
subtopics: Reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning optimization
Neuro-symbolic and structured logical reasoning
Memory and state management for LLM agents
Evaluation and benchmarking of reasoning capabilities
Test-time compute scaling and inference efficiency

24.label: AI Fairness, Causality, and Explainability
24.description: This cluster encompasses research on making AI systems more transparent, fair, and causally grounded, spanning explainable AI methods, algorithmic fairness mechanisms, causal inference and representation learning, and interpretable decision-making in applied domains such as finance and ecology.
subtopics: Explainable AI techniques and interpretability methods
Algorithmic fairness, bias mitigation, and fairness-aware decision-making
Causal inference, causal representation learning, and counterfactual reasoning
Multimodal and interpretable financial forecasting and trading
Influence functions, feature attribution, and model transparency

25.label: Federated Learning and Machine Unlearning
25.description: Research on distributed, privacy-preserving machine learning frameworks—including federated learning, split learning, and machine unlearning—addressing challenges of communication efficiency, data heterogeneity, privacy, and model utility.
subtopics: Federated learning communication efficiency and aggregation methods
Machine unlearning for generative AI and graph neural networks
Split and hierarchical federated learning for resource-constrained devices
Privacy-preserving distributed training and differential privacy
Data heterogeneity and non-IID challenges in federated settings
